name: DCOUNTA
description: DCOUNTA counts the non-blank cells in a specified field of the database records that match the given criteria. Unlike DCOUNT, it counts text as well as numbers.
tldr: Counts non-blank values in a database column for rows that meet the criteria.

parameters.name: database
parameters.description: The range containing the database, including the header row as the first row.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: The column to count, given as the column label in quotes (e.g. "Tree") or its 1-based column index.

parameters.name: criteria
parameters.description: The range with a header row matching database column names and one or more condition rows; only matching records are counted.

basicExample.description: Count non-blank Tree values for apple trees taller than 10
basicExample.explanation: The criteria A9:B10 matches two rows; the Tree field is non-blank (text) in both, so DCOUNTA counts 2.

advancedExamples.title: DCOUNTA vs DCOUNT on a text field
advancedExamples.description: DCOUNT returns 0 on a text field, but DCOUNTA counts the non-blank text entries.
advancedExamples.explanation: Both matching rows have a Tree label, so DCOUNTA returns 2 while DCOUNT would return 0.

advancedExamples.title: Count all apple-tree records
advancedExamples.description: Use criteria A9:A10 to count every non-blank field cell among apple rows.
advancedExamples.explanation: Three apple rows exist, each with a non-blank numeric Yield, so the count is 3.

howItWorks: DCOUNTA filters the database to rows matching the criteria, then counts how many of those rows have a non-blank value in the specified field column. Both text and numbers are counted; only empty cells are excluded.

howToSteps.name: Set up the database
howToSteps.text: Enter your table with a header row, e.g. A1:E7 with Tree, Height, Age, Yield, Profit.

howToSteps.name: Set up criteria
howToSteps.text: Place criteria headers and values in a separate range, e.g. A9:B10.

limitations: Counts any non-blank cell, including text, so it is not limited to numbers like DCOUNT.
Truly empty cells in the field are not counted.
Criteria header labels must exactly match database headers.

commonErrors.cause: No rows matched the criteria, or the field was entirely blank in matching rows.
commonErrors.fix: Verify the criteria headers and conditions match the database.

commonErrors.cause: The field was an unquoted column name.
commonErrors.fix: Wrap the field name in quotes, e.g. "Tree", or use the column index.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: DCOUNTA works identically in Google Sheets with the same arguments and behavior.

faq.question: How is DCOUNTA different from DCOUNT?
faq.answer: DCOUNT counts only numeric cells; DCOUNTA counts any non-blank cell, including text.

faq.question: Does DCOUNTA count empty cells?
faq.answer: No. Only non-blank cells in the field of matching rows are counted.

faq.question: When should I use DCOUNTA?
faq.answer: Use it when you need to tally matching records regardless of whether the field holds numbers or text.
